title: Procurement exec readout + pricing / SSO handoff
summary: Executive procurement readout: high-level procurement questions about MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, SSO/KMS integration, pricing approval path. SE demo preflight and benchmark ask to validate latency/cost. Clear next steps: send annotated redlines, SOC2 + network diagram, pricing worksheet for committed tiers, schedule technical preflight/bench on dedicated vs hosted models.
topics: Pricing approval path and commit tiers
Private deployment vs Hosted API tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-04
- Start: 16:00 PST
- Duration approx 52m
- Recording: enabled
- Attendees: Lena, Marco, Aisha (Redwood); Jason, Priya, Tom, Renee (Cobalt)

Summary (auto): Lena provides commercial readout, Priya focuses on legal redlines and logging/audit, Tom wants network/egress details, Jason and Renee want pricing path to present to committee.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everybody, thanks for joining, uh we know you all are tight on time so we'll run the readout and then hand off to Marco for a short tech preflight.
[00:14] Jason Patel: Yeah thanks Lena, appreciate it. I have the procurement committee in the loop but wanted to get the legal and technical clarity before we push for pricing approval next week.
[00:28] Priya Menon: Quick clarity, we already flagged three DPA clauses — data residency, subprocessors, and deletion timelines — I want to confirm Redwood's standard positions and where we can expect redlines.
[00:40] Lena Park: For sure. On the DPA, our standard is 30-day data deletion for transient inference logs, with options for longer retention in Dedicated or Private deployments. But we can annotate the MSA/DPA and call out exceptions. We'll send an annotated doc with proposed language.
[00:58] Renee Wu: When you say "Dedicated or Private deployments", can you confirm if that affects pricing and thumbs on egress fees? We're very sensitive to predictable billing.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: (SE) yeah, good q — Dedicated gives reserved capacity which stabilizes unit cost. Egress is still cloud egress from the region, so you'll see network fees. For Private on-prem we can avoid cloud egress but there's a one-time deploy fee and support contract.
[01:30] Tom Ellis: So if we need KMS integration — our keys are in vault, HSM-backed — do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[01:42] Lena Park: We do KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated; hosted has KMS support via a managed key option and enterprise customers can request bring-your-own-key (BYOK) workflows — it's in the security appendix. We'll attach the KMS playbook link. Link: https://redwood.ai/security/kms-playbook
[01:58] Priya Menon: Also need audit logs and immutable trails for compliance. Can you commit to log retention and paper trail for audit?
[02:10] Marco Ruiz: We emit audit logs for all major operations — key rotations, model deployments, admin role changes — retention is configurable, and we can export syslog to your SIEM. Note: there's a standard retention of 90 days on hosted unless extended via add-on.
[02:32] Priya Menon: Okay we will need at least 12 months retention for certain endpoints, can you put that as an option in the redlines.
[02:40] Lena Park: Absolutely. We'll mark that as an optional clause that goes to procurement/finance for delta pricing.

[03:05] Jason Patel: On the pricing workflow — our committee needs a clear committed usage tier to evaluate. Renee, do you want reserved spend or on-demand?
[03:16] Renee Wu: Ideally a two-phase approach: pilot on hosted on-demand to validate, then commit to Dedicated for production. But we need the delta numbers — per-token unit when reserved at 500k/month vs on-demand.
[03:31] Lena Park: Got it. We'll send a pricing worksheet showing on-demand vs reserved at tiers: 100k/500k/2M tokens with egress and KMS add-on line items. Expect a workbook and a short one-pager.

[03:50] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot we recommend sampling your peak flows — chat sessions at 2k tokens/session — we'll run a small benchmark. For hosted that's 1-2ms per token on our cluster for the base config, but for long-tail bursts we advise a dedicated pool. Note: transcripts sometimes show KV cash instead of KV cache in our automated notes, ignore that typo.
[04:22] Tom Ellis: On the technical preflight: what network ports, CIDR whitelisting, and SSO flows do you need?
[04:30] Marco Ruiz: We usually request egress to our control plane on 443 only, and we provide a list of IP ranges for whitelisting. SSO via SAML OK, SCIM for provisioning. We'll share a connectivity checklist.
[04:49] Priya Menon: Does the MSA include a standard SOC2 paragraph? We need to evaluate evidence.
[04:56] Lena Park: Yes, SOC2 type II is included in our attestation. We'll attach the cert and the network diagram (redacted). Link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-cert 

[05:20] Renee Wu: Finance question — if we go Dedicated and underutilize, is there any flex or burn-down clause? We can't overcommit without visibility.
[05:30] Lena Park: Our reserved contracts have a 12-month minimum with an option for quarterly review and a one-time adjustment window at month 6. There is also a burst policy for temporary spikes. We'll call out the burn-down credit policy in the worksheet.

[05:50] Jason Patel: Who will be our escalation contact for SLO breaches? Need a clear SLA and penalty structure to show to the board.
[05:59] Lena Park: SLA contacts: primary CSM (Aisha) and SE escalation (Marco). We support SLOs by tier and have uptime credits for missed targets. We'll include a sample SLA appendix.

[06:12] Aisha Khan: I'll be the CSM contact, I'll set up access to the console and invite your team for the trial.

[06:20] Marco Ruiz: Quick tech note — for heavy KV-cache workloads we recommend quantized model variants; that reduces memory and cost but may slightly change output distribution. We'll include model recommendations.

[06:40] Priya Menon: Redlines on indemnity and IP — we prefer mutual indemnification and limited liability; your MSA looked our way a little more vendor-favorable.
[06:53] Lena Park: Understood. We'll ask legal to mark up mutual indemnity language and propose a compromise on cap of liability anchored to the annual contract value.

[07:10] Tom Ellis: Are there any export control or classification issues we need to be aware of? We operate in APAC and EMEA and must ensure data residency.
[07:21] Lena Park: We support region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports on-prem deployment in EMEA or APAC. Export controls are in the DPA and we can discuss addendums for sensitive data.

[07:40] Jason Patel: Okay let's pivot — Marco, can you walk us through a 10 minute checklist for the preflight? We need to know what you'll test in the pilot.

[07:48] Marco Ruiz: Sure. I'll keep it high level — connectivity checklist, auth (SAML/SCIM), KMS connectivity test, model payloads, latency / p95 measurements under synthetic load, KV-cache validation, and a small security scan. We'll need a test account and a sample dataset that doesn't contain PII.

[08:30] Priya Menon: On PII — we can't use production PII, but we will provide a masked sample set. Also, for the records, any logs containing sensitive tokens must be redacted.

[08:45] Marco Ruiz: Agreed — we'll only use masked data. Also note that our logs are hashed and we can provide masking steps in the checklist.

[09:05] Renee Wu: Timing: if we get the redlines and pricing by Friday, our committee meets Monday and we could sign off. Is that timeline doable?
[09:15] Lena Park: Yes we can target sending annotated MSA/DPA and pricing workbook by Friday EOD. We should get the preflight scheduled for next Wed/Thu.

[09:30] Jason Patel: Ok, procedure for the legal play: Priya will submit the redlines, we need Redwood legal to respond within 3 business days. Can you commit to that?
[09:40] Lena Park: We'll prioritize it — our legal typically responds within 3-5 business days for enterprise redlines; we'll escalate for the committee timeline.

[10:00] Priya Menon: A couple of specific asks: 1) can you accommodate a 45-day deletion instead of 30? 2) ability to get immutable audit export for up to 12 months? 3) SAML attribute mapping for groups?

[10:20] Marco Ruiz: 1) deletion 45 days is ok as a paid option. 2) export for 12 months — yes via our add-on. 3) SAML mapping — we support attribute mapping and group sync via SCIM; some attribute names vary but we can map in our admin console.

[11:01] Jason Patel: Great — Rene, anything else from finance?
[11:06] Renee Wu: We'll want the workbook to show TCO over 12 months, best/worst case with egress and KMS. Also show the monthly burn vs committed number for ease of reporting.

[11:26] Aisha Khan: We'll include a 12-month TCO tab and a delta row for egress & keying.

[11:35] Tom Ellis: On SLA credits — is it automatic or do we need to file a claim? Sometimes vendors require a claim process which wastes time.

[11:45] Lena Park: It's an automated credit for some tiers; for others you file a claim with evidence. We'll clarify which is automatic and set the claim window in the appendix.

[12:05] Priya Menon: Also need to confirm that subprocessor list and notification windows are adequate. We require 30 days notice of any new subprocessors.

[12:13] Lena Park: Redwood provides a subprocessor list and commit to 30-day notice; any objections can create exceptions.

[12:28] Marco Ruiz: Back to the bench plan — we'll need a 2-hour window with your staging workload to capture realistic latencies. We'll forward a runbook and sample load generator.

[12:48] Jason Patel: Ok, so to recap the high level commitments and next steps, Priya do you want to add legal expectations?

[13:00] Priya Menon: Legal expects annotated redlines, SOC2 evidence, KMS procedure, and a statement on audit log immutability. We'll need these to route to our compliance team.

[13:12] Lena Park: We'll deliver annotated MSA/DPA, SOC2 cert, the KMS playbook link, network diagram, and the pricing workbook by Friday EOD. Aisha will set up the technical preflight and Marco will run the bench.

[13:30] Jason Patel: Can we also get an itemized list of what production monitoring looks like and access for our oncall to escalate?

[13:38] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we'll share the observability dashboard screenshot and SLO alerting playbook. You can integrate alerts to your pager system via webhook.

[13:55] Renee Wu: One more: when we present to the committee, is Redwood open to a conditional pilot clause where production enablement is contingent on passing bench results?

[14:06] Lena Park: Yes that is a standard pilot-to-prod gating clause. We'll include acceptance criteria in the pilot statement.

[14:25] Jason Patel: Great. Anything else?

[14:32] Tom Ellis: I did want to flag we may request a temporary escalation SIEM access for the pilot proof — read-only. Is that possible?

[14:44] Marco Ruiz: Read-only SIEM export is possible via syslog or S3 dumps; we can set a timebound access token. We'll document the flow.

[15:02] Priya Menon: Okay, Lena, please make sure legal names are exact on the redline doc and include the reporting cadence (monthly) and the audit contact.

[15:12] Lena Park: Will do. Aisha will own invites for the weekly pilot sync. Marco and I will follow up with redlines and the workbook.

[15:25] Jason Patel: Thanks everyone — just to be clear on deadlines: redlines & pricing by Friday, bench scheduled next Wed, committee review Monday.

[15:35] Lena Park: Yes. I'll capture action items and follow up after the call. Thanks all.
